gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-osmanya: Noto Sans Osmanya reads with wide, easy s turns and a lowercase that looms large beside its capitals, a friendly workhorse under Warnes. Warnes is the wild one here, every stroke the same width and tapering away.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmong: Warnes draws every stroke like bent wire, stretched wide with tapered ends that never quite touch. And Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong follows with a high x-height and gapped rounds, so paragraphs stay quiet and easy to follow.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-palmyrene: Expressive is the right word for Warnes, whose marker-like strokes ignore direction, while Noto Sans Palmyrene keeps its curves stopping short and ascenders compact. Bigger headings suit it.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-samaritan: Warnes looks like bent paperclips, loose and bold. Noto Sans Samaritan has a hefty lowercase and curves with plenty of daylight inside, so a long page of text feels sturdy and welcoming.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-saurashtra: Warnes stretches wide with one stroke width throughout. Noto Sans Saurashtra, a plain sans with barely taller capitals and open counters, would feel lost if the heading were shrunk down small.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-sunuwar: Rope-like curves, loose and bold, define Warnes, tapered and widely spaced. And Noto Sans Sunuwar brings open curves and short ascender stems, a plain sans that lets the heading's wiry swagger breathe.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-syloti-nagri: Warnes is monoline and expressive, its stretched letters tapering out before they touch. And Noto Sans Syloti Nagri brings short ascenders, a tall x-height and an open-bowled a, which is the pair's strongest hook.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-tagalog: Wire-straight and wide, Warnes makes the first impression. Noto Sans Tagalog, a sans with a dominant middle zone and generous curve gaps, is the pair's strongest card, giving the heading plenty of calm room.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-tai-tham: Expressive Warnes draws smooth, unflared strokes with no pinched joints, and shines in big display moments. Noto Sans Tai Tham, a sans-serif with crowded chalk-board lowercase and visible c insides, handles steady text.
gen-gf-warnes-gf-noto-sans-tc: Wire-like and bold, Warnes stretches its tapering strokes wide across the line, with spacing to match. Noto Sans TC, a sans-serif, opens its large counters outward, a gentle foil.
